project_name: Update LARAP for PLTP Mataloko (20 MW) and PLTP Ulumbu (20 MW) Geothermal Power Plant Project – KfW Development Bank
description:
As part of the development of the Mataloko 20 MW and Ulumbu 20 MW geothermal power plants in Flores Island, this consultancy assignment involves updating the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) for the entire project scope, including ancillary infrastructure such as transmission lines, access roads, borrow/pit areas, worker camps and staging zones. 
Our work includes:

  • Socio-economic surveys, census and asset inventories (IOL), with gender-responsive elements. 

  • Stakeholder engagement planning (SEP), Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes with Indigenous Peoples, grievance redress mechanism (GRM) design. 

  • Detailed update of LARAP including institutional arrangements, implementation roadmap, livelihood restoration measures, and disclosure of findings. 

By delivering robust social and environmental safeguards documentation and implementation-ready plans, the project supports PT PLN in executing the geothermal power projects in a socially responsible, transparent and sustainable manner.
client_name: PT PLN (Persero) – UIP Nusra

project_name: External Social Safeguard Monitoring for CW - 1, 2, 3, 4A and 4B Under Flood Management in Selected River Basin Sector Project (FMSRBSP)
description:
As part of the Flood Management in Selected River Basin Sector Project (FMSRBSP), this work package provides independent External Social Safeguard Monitoring for construction packages CW-1, CW-2, CW-3, CW-4A, and CW-4B in Banten and Maluku Provinces.

The monitoring activities include verification of land acquisition and resettlement instruments, assessment of Land Acquisition and Resettlement Plan (LARP) implementation, evaluation of livelihood restoration, verification of grievance redress mechanisms, and review of social mitigation measures at household and community levels.

The methodology involves field verification, database validation (including Detailed Measurement Survey / Inventory of Losses), and stakeholder interviews. Monitoring results are presented through periodic reports containing findings, strategic recommendations, and implementation improvements to strengthen compliance with national policy frameworks and ADB safeguard standards, ensuring that flood management investments are implemented in an accountable, equitable, and sustainable manner.
client_name: Ministry of Public Works

project_name: Socio-economic Baseline Survey for ESIA, LARAP and SEP Preparation for the Indonesia Batam‑Bintan
description: As part of the preparation phase for the Batam-Bintan Bridge Project, this consultancy service conducts a comprehensive socio-economic baseline survey to support the development of the Environmental & Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP), and the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP). The survey covers affected households and communities in Batam Island and Bintan Island, capturing gender-disaggregated socio-economic data, vulnerable groups, land and asset ownership, livelihood conditions, and community perceptions. Findings will form the basis for compensation frameworks, livelihood restoration programs, grievance redress mechanisms (GRM), and stakeholder consultation strategies. By establishing a robust baseline, the project ensures alignment with national regulations and international safeguard requirements, thereby fostering inclusive, transparent and sustainable implementation of the Batam-Bintan bridge infrastructure.
client_name: PT Bita Bina Semesta - ARUP, AIIB as Project Beneficiary

project_name: Location Determination and Land Acquisition Planning Documents — Penlok Bahodopi & Penlok/LARAP-FEL3 (ESIA) Pomalaa
description:
In support of the strategic nickel-smelting and processing development at Bahodopi (Central Sulawesi) and Pomalaa (Southeast Sulawesi), this consultancy assignment provides independent services for location determination (Penlok), preparation of land acquisition planning documents (LARAP/FEL3), and Environmental & Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for the two sites.
The scope includes:

  • Determining and validating optimal locations for project infrastructure at Bahodopi and Pomalaa (Penlok tasks).

  • Conducting land acquisition planning (LARAP/FEL3) including inventory of losses, entitlement frameworks, and resettlement strategy.

  • Undertaking ESIA in alignment with national and international safeguard standards—assessing environmental and social risks, stakeholder impacts, and mitigation measures.

  • Designing grievance redress mechanism (GRM) and stakeholder engagement plan (SEP) to ensure community participation and responsiveness during land acquisition, relocation or compensation processes.

  • Supporting the client in obtaining necessary environmental permits and aligning with regulatory and corporate sustainability requirements.

By combining technical land-acquisition planning and high standards of social and environmental safeguards, the consultancy ensures that the Bahodopi and Pomalaa developments are structured with a foundation of responsible social license, equitable compensation, and sustainable community relations.
client_name: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk

project_name: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of LARAP Study and Land Acquisition Planning Documents – Matenggeng Pumped Storage 943 MW
description:
The MPSPP project is planned to have a capacity of 943 MW, located in Ciamis Regency and Kuningan Regency in West Java Province, as well as Cilacap Regency in Central Java Province. This project includes the construction of an Upper Dam and a Lower Dam, which are located on the Cimancing River and the Citetel River, respectively, both of which flow into the Cijolang River, a tributary of the Citanduy River.

Objectives

The primary objective is to prepare a comprehensive Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) for the Matenggeng Pumped Storage Power Plant Project. This plan will be developed in full alignment with the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5: Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement) and relevant Indonesian laws and regulations, including Law No. 2 of 2012 concerning Land Acquisition for Public Interest Development and its derivative regulations. The LARAP will serve as a strategic and operational guide to ensure that the land acquisition and resettlement process is implemented transparently and equitably, mitigates adverse socio-economic impacts, and ensures that Project-Affected Persons (PAPs) receive fair compensation and assistance to improve, or at a minimum, restore their livelihoods and standards of living to pre-project levels.

Scope of Services

The scope of service covers all necessary stages for LARAP preparation and planning, ensuring compliance with both Indonesian law and World Bank ESS5 standards. The activities include:

  • Identification and Mapping of Affected Areas: Conducting a detailed identification and mapping of all land parcels and assets within the project's footprint, covering the Upper and Lower Dams, supporting facilities (access roads, quarries), and the 30 km, 500 kV transmission line corridor, including its Right-of-Way (RoW).
  • Socio-economic Survey and Vulnerability Assessment: Executing a comprehensive census and Inventory of Losses (IOL) for all PAPs to gather baseline socio-economic data. This scope includes identifying vulnerable groups (such as low-income households, the elderly, female-headed households, and indigenous groups) who may require additional assistance.
  • Public Consultation and Information Disclosure: Planning and implementing a meaningful consultation process with PAPs and other stakeholders throughout the LARAP preparation. This includes disclosing relevant project information in an accessible and understandable format to ensure their participation in the planning process, as mandated by both frameworks.
  • Formulation of the Entitlement Matrix and Valuation: Developing a detailed entitlement matrix that bridges any gaps between Indonesian regulations and World Bank ESS5 requirements. This matrix will define the eligibility for compensation and other assistance for each category of loss, ensuring that compensation for assets is provided at full replacement cost and is considered "layak dan adil" (proper and fair) according to national law.
  • Resettlement and Livelihood Restoration Planning: Designing a comprehensive Resettlement Plan for physically displaced households and a Livelihood Restoration Program for all eligible PAPs. The program will be designed to improve or at least restore income levels and living standards through tailored support, such as agricultural assistance, skills training, or access to credit.
  • Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM): Establishing a project-specific GRM that is culturally appropriate, accessible, and responsive. The mechanism will be available to all PAPs, including vulnerable groups, at no cost, to address and resolve project-related concerns and grievances effectively.
  • Implementation Plan, Budget, and Monitoring Framework: Developing a detailed implementation schedule, a comprehensive budget for all LARAP activities (including compensation and restoration programs), and a framework for internal and external monitoring and evaluation to ensure the LARAP objectives are successfully met.
client_name: Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM) - PT PLN (Persero)  - Central Java Development Unit (UIP JBT)

project_name: Consultancy Services on Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) Phase II — Mentarang Induk Hydroelectric Project (MIHEP)
description:
As part of the development of the Mentarang Induk Hydroelectric Project (MIHEP) in North Kalimantan, this consultancy encompasses the second-phase study of the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP). The assignment addresses significant resettlement impacts — both physical displacement and economic loss — arising from the project’s large-scale hydropower facility and associated infrastructure. The scope includes designing compensation policies, livelihood restoration programmes, validating land acquisition procedures, assessing host-community interactions, consulting affected persons, and establishing grievance redress and dispute resolution mechanisms. The study is conducted in compliance with Indonesian legal frameworks and aligned with international best-practice standards such as the Hydropower Sustainability Guidelines, IFC Performance Standards, and the Equator Principles.

Through these efforts, the project supports PT Kayan Hydropower Nusantara in building a structured and equitable resettlement framework that safeguards the rights and welfare of affected communities, ensures transparent land acquisition, delivers fair compensation, restores livelihoods, and strengthens community resilience — thereby embedding social sustainability into the broader hydropower initiative.
client_name: PT Kayan Hydropower Nusantara — a joint-venture between Alamtri Resources Indonesia/Adaro, Sarawak Energy Berhad, and KPP Group

project_name: Preparation of Land Acquisition Planning Document (DPPT) and Feasibility Study for Kamal (North Jakarta) and Rawa Lindung (South Jakarta) Reservoir Development Plan
description:
This consultancy project supports the Jakarta Provincial Government through the Department of Water Resources (Dinas SDA) in preparing the Feasibility Study and Land Acquisition Planning Document (DPPT) for the proposed development of Kamal Reservoir in North Jakarta and Rawa Lindung Reservoir in South Jakarta. The study aims to evaluate the technical, environmental, and socio-economic feasibility of the reservoir development, including land acquisition requirements, resettlement implications, and environmental management measures.

The DPPT component involves mapping affected land parcels, identifying ownership, and estimating compensation needs in accordance with Indonesia’s land acquisition regulations and social safeguard principles. The feasibility study further assesses hydrological functions, engineering design alternatives, and potential social and environmental impacts.

By integrating technical, social, and environmental analyses, this project provides a comprehensive planning framework to support sustainable urban water management and flood control infrastructure in Jakarta.
client_name: Water Resources Agency; Local Government of DKI Jakarta

project_name: Consultancy Services for the Preparation of DP3 (Dokumen Proposal Proyek Prakarsa) – Pluit to Airport Toll Road (Pluit–Bandara) and Utilities
description:
Within the strategic initiative to develop the Pluit–Bandara toll road corridor and associated utility works, this consultancy engagement supports the preparation of the DP3 (Dokumen Proposal Proyek Prakarsa) and associated land acquisition planning documents (DPPT). The scope of work involves:

  • Preparing the DPPT as an integral input to the DP3, detailing land acquisition strategy, land use change implications, utilities relocation requirements and preliminary schedule for acquisition and clearing.

  • Conducting baseline assessment of existing land parcels, utilities infrastructure, rights-of-way, and impacted assets along the Pluit–Bandara corridor (spanning portions of DKI Jakarta and Banten).

  • Engaging key stakeholders—public authorities, utility providers, local communities—and establishing the grievance redress mechanism (GRM) specific to land acquisition and utilities relocation.

  • Advising on implementation planning, cost estimates for land acquisition and utilities relocation, ensuring alignment with Indonesian regulatory framework and best practice for toll-road infrastructure development.

Through rigorous planning and stakeholder alignment, this consultancy aims to equip PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada Tbk with a robust DP3/DPPT package that enhances project readiness, accelerates land acquisition and utilities relocation, and supports the eventual construction phase of the Pluit–Bandara toll road corridor with minimized delays and socially responsible implementation.
client_name: PT Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada Tbk (CMNP)

project_name: External Monitoring pada Consulting Service for The Construction Supervision of Patimban Access Toll Road Construction Project JICA Loan No. IP-586
description:
As part of the Consulting Service for the Construction Supervision of the Patimban Access Toll Road Construction Project, this activity focuses on External Monitoring of Safeguards to ensure that project implementation aligns with the principles of sustainability, social compliance, and protection of affected communities. The monitoring is conducted independently, referring to both national policy frameworks and the applicable safeguard standards of the lending agency.

The scope of work includes monitoring the progress of land acquisition and relocation, assessing the implementation of the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP), evaluating livelihood restoration, verifying grievance redress mechanisms, and mitigating social impacts at the household and community levels.

Monitoring results are presented through periodic reports complemented by strategic recommendations and implementation improvements based on field findings. This approach aims to ensure that the Patimban Toll Road development not only achieves its construction targets but is also carried out in an accountable, equitable manner, and in accordance with the principles of responsible social impact management.
client_name: PT Virama Karya (Persero) KSO PT Anugerah Krida Pradana, PT Java CM & PT Wahana Mitra Amerta - Ministry of Public Works and Housing (Direktorat Jenderal Bina Marga) as Project Beneficiary

project_name: Consultancy Services on Land Acquisition and Livelihood Restoration Plan (LALRP) Study for the Mentarang Induk Hydroelectric Project – Overhead Transmission Line
description:
As part of the development of the Mentarang Induk Hydroelectric Project (MIHEP) and its 500 kV overhead transmission line, this consultancy provides an independent Land Acquisition and Livelihood Restoration Plan (LALRP) Study to ensure that land acquisition and social safeguard processes are implemented in a transparent, equitable, and sustainable manner.

The assignment covers a comprehensive assessment of land acquisition impacts and socio-economic conditions of affected communities, validation of the Detailed Measurement Survey (DMS) and Inventory of Losses (IOL), formulation of livelihood restoration strategies, and development of frameworks for grievance redress, stakeholder engagement, and social monitoring. It also integrates aspects of Cultural Heritage Management (CHMP) and Indigenous Peoples Planning (IPP) to ensure full compliance with Indonesian regulations and international best-practice safeguard standards for hydropower infrastructure.

Deliverables include the preparation of the LALRP document, implementation roadmap, and recommendations to guide the client in executing land acquisition and restoration programs in alignment with both national requirements and international expectations for responsible and socially inclusive project development.

Through evidence-based analysis and field engagement, the study supports PT Kayan Hydropower Nusantara in realizing the MIHEP’s vision as a strategic national project (PSN) that delivers renewable energy while upholding social responsibility and sustainable community development in North Kalimantan.
client_name: PT Kayan Hydropower Nusantara – a joint venture of Alamtri (Adaro Group), Sarawak Energy Berhad, and KPP Group

project_name: Social Safeguard, LARAP and Gender-Responsive Analysis for Raw Water Intake and Transmission Systems (Kertasari & Jatigede in West Java; Lau Simeme in North Sumatra)
description:
Within the programme to strengthen raw water supply infrastructure in Indonesia—covering the Kertasari system (West Java), the Jatigede Stage II system (West Java) and the Lau Simeme reservoir / transmission system (North Sumatra)—this consultancy provides independent social safeguard, land acquisition and livelihood-restoration planning support. The assignment includes a comprehensive survey and analysis of affected land and assets, preparation of the LARAP and DPPT documents, gender-responsive analysis of community and household impacts, stakeholder engagement, asset/crop inventory (IOL), and grievance redress mechanism design.

Methodology combines field verification, demographic and socio-economic data collection (with gender-disaggregated indicators), mapping of land-use and ownership, assessment of community impacts of infrastructure intake and transmission works, and formulation of mitigation and restoration measures aligned with both Indonesian regulatory framework and international safeguard standards (for example, Asian Development Bank Safeguard Policy Statement).

Outputs include:

  • Detailed LARAP reports and a DPPT (Land Acquisition Planning Document) for each system (Kertasari, Jatigede, Lau Simeme)

  • Gender-responsive analysis report integrating the impacts on women, vulnerable groups and decision-making processes at household level

  • Stakeholder engagement and grievance redress mechanism framework

  • Socio-economic baseline and inventory of losses (land, buildings, crops)

  • Strategic recommendations to support safe, equitable and sustainable implementation of the raw-water infrastructure investments

This work supports the aim of ensuring that the raw-water intake and transmission systems are not only technically and financially viable, but also socially responsible—ensuring fair compensation, livelihood restoration, gender equity, community participation and minimal negative social impacts.
client_name: Directorate General of Human Settlements (DGHS), Directorate General of Water Resources (DGWR), MPWH
partner_name: Oriental Consultants Global Co., Ltd. (on behalf of relevant implementing agencies)

project_name: Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and supplementary studies in accordance with the international standards (Equator Principles and IFC Performance Standards)
description: This assignment involves conducting a comprehensive Environmental & Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and associated safeguard studies for the industrial/nickel processing development by IHIP & HNI in South Sulawesi. The consultancy covers the preparation of LARAP, surveys of social, economic and land acquisition impacts, stakeholder engagement, grievance redress mechanism (GRM) design, and assurance of compliance with the international standards (Equator Principles and IFC Performance Standards). The goal is to support the client in implementing the project in a socially responsible and environmentally sustainable manner, ensuring that land acquisition, resettlement, community impacts and environmental risks are managed to international best practice.
client_name: PT Indonesia Huali Industry Park (IHIP) and PT Huali Nickel Indonesia (HNI)

project_name: Preparation of Land Acquisition Planning Document (DPPT) and Feasibility Study for Kebagusan (South Jakarta), Jati Kramat (East Jakarta), and Duren Tiga (South Jakarta) Reservoir Development Plan
description:
This consultancy supports the Jakarta Provincial Government’s Department of Water Resources (Dinas SDA) in the preparation of the Feasibility Study (FS) and Land Acquisition Planning Documents (DPPT) for the proposed development of three strategic urban reservoirs: Kebagusan, Jati Kramat, and Duren Tiga.

The study aims to assess the technical, environmental, and socio-economic feasibility of reservoir construction as part of Jakarta’s flood mitigation and water resource management initiatives. The DPPT component focuses on identifying affected land parcels, ownership structures, and estimating compensation requirements in compliance with Indonesia’s land acquisition framework and social safeguard principles.

Through integrated analysis covering engineering, environmental, and social aspects, this project provides a comprehensive planning foundation for sustainable urban reservoir development—supporting improved flood control capacity, groundwater recharge, and water security in Jakarta.
client_name: Department of Water Resources (Dinas SDA), Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta

project_name: Preparation of Masterplan Document, KKPR and Industrial Business License (IUI/IUKI) Management for Takalar Industrial Area
description:
This consultancy focuses on the preparation of the masterplan document and management of spatial and licensing requirements for the development of the Takalar Industrial Area in South Sulawesi. The assignment includes preparing the Feasibility Study (FS), obtaining the KKPR (Kesesuaian Kegiatan Pemanfaatan Ruang), and managing the Industrial Business License (IUI/IUKI) process in accordance with national regulations and regional development policies.

The project aims to provide a comprehensive spatial, technical, and regulatory framework to support the sustainable growth of Takalar’s industrial zone as a strategic regional investment hub. The study covers site suitability analysis, infrastructure layout planning, environmental and social considerations, and integration with local economic development programs.

Through this work, the consultancy supports the acceleration of industrial area readiness by ensuring compliance with Indonesia’s licensing system (OSS RBA), enhancing investment feasibility, and promoting balanced industrial development aligned with environmental and spatial governance principles.
client_name: Masterplan Document Preparation Work Takalar Industrial Area, KKPR and IUKI Management

project_name: Land Analysis and Soil Sample Collection Project in Central and East Java
description:
This project involves conducting a comprehensive land and soil suitability analysis to support the feasibility study for agricultural and plantation development across selected sites in Central and East Java. The consultancy covers field survey, soil sample collection, laboratory testing, and spatial land evaluation to determine the physical and chemical characteristics of the soil and its suitability for various crop types and land uses.

The analysis focuses on parameters such as soil texture, fertility, drainage capacity, pH levels, organic content, and topography—integrated with GIS-based mapping and spatial data interpretation. Results from the study will inform land-use planning, agricultural investment decisions, and sustainable resource management strategies within the target plantation areas.

By combining scientific precision and spatial analytics, this project provides clients with reliable baseline data for optimizing land utilization and ensuring environmentally responsible plantation planning in line with sustainable agriculture principles.
client_name: PT Eidara Matadata Presisi – PT Riset Perkebunan Nusantara

project_name: Preparation of Environmental Impact Assessment (AMDAL) Document for the Rongkong Multipurpose Dam Project, South Sulawesi
description:
This consultancy focuses on the preparation of the Environmental Impact Assessment (AMDAL) and supporting documentation for the Rongkong Multipurpose Dam Project located in South Sulawesi. The assignment covers comprehensive environmental baseline studies, impact prediction and evaluation, public consultation processes, and the formulation of mitigation and monitoring plans to ensure that the dam development complies with both Indonesian environmental regulations and international good practice.

The study assesses potential impacts on river hydrology, water quality, aquatic ecosystems, terrestrial biodiversity, land use, and social conditions within the project area. It also includes preparation of the Environmental Management Plan (RKL) and Environmental Monitoring Plan (RPL), along with documentation required for the Environmental Permit (Izin Lingkungan).

By integrating engineering, environmental, and socio-economic considerations, this project aims to provide a scientifically sound and regulatory-compliant environmental framework that supports sustainable and responsible dam construction and operation in the Rongkong River Basin.
client_name: ACE Pvt. Ltd. (in Joint Venture)

project_name: Training and Workshop on Procedures for Implementing Land Acquisition for Development for the Public Interest – PLN UPDL Makassar (Phase I)
description:
This project involved the design and delivery of a training and workshop program focused on the procedures and regulatory framework for land acquisition for development in the public interest (Pengadaan Tanah bagi Pembangunan untuk Kepentingan Umum), in collaboration with PLN UPDL Makassar.

The training provided participants with a comprehensive understanding of the legal, administrative, and technical procedures in land acquisition under Indonesian Law No. 2/2012 and its implementing regulations. The program also emphasized stakeholder coordination, compensation mechanisms, grievance redress management (GRM), and social safeguard practices relevant to infrastructure and energy sector projects.

Through interactive sessions and case-based discussions, the workshop strengthened the institutional and practical capacity of PLN personnel in managing land acquisition efficiently, transparently, and in compliance with both national laws and social safeguard principles.
client_name: PT PLN (Persero) – UPDL Makassar

project_name: IFC Gap Fulfilment (ESIA–LARAP Study) for the Pomalaa High Pressure Acid Leach (HPAL) Nickel Project
description:
This consultancy supports the Pomalaa High Pressure Acid Leach (HPAL) Nickel Project by conducting an IFC Gap Fulfilment Study focused on environmental and social safeguards. The work involves a comprehensive review and update of the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) to ensure full compliance with the IFC Performance Standards, the Equator Principles, and Indonesia’s environmental and social regulations.

The assignment includes field verification, socio-economic and stakeholder consultations, environmental baseline assessment, gap analysis between existing studies and IFC requirements, and preparation of corrective action plans. The project aims to strengthen the safeguard framework of PT Vale Indonesia’s nickel development operations, ensuring responsible land acquisition, transparent community engagement, and sustainable environmental management throughout the project lifecycle.

By aligning project documentation and practices with international sustainability standards, this study contributes to the environmental and social due diligence required for international financing and reinforces PT Vale Indonesia’s commitment to ethical, transparent, and sustainable mining operations.
client_name: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk

project_name: Due Diligence and LARAP Preparation for the Pomalaa High Pressure Acid Leach (HPAL) Nickel Project – International Finance Corporation (IFC)
description:
This consultancy provides social safeguard due diligence and LARAP preparation services for the Pomalaa HPAL Nickel Project, a strategic nickel processing initiative developed by PT Vale in Southeast Sulawesi. The assignment is carried out in alignment with IFC Performance Standards, Equator Principles, and Indonesian regulatory frameworks governing land acquisition and resettlement.

The study involves verifying land acquisition processes, identifying project-affected persons and assets, assessing livelihood impacts, and preparing the Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) consistent with IFC requirements. Additionally, it includes stakeholder consultations, grievance redress mechanism (GRM) development, and the formulation of corrective action plans to bridge gaps between national procedures and international best practice.

Through this due diligence process, the project ensures that land acquisition and resettlement activities for the Pomalaa HPAL facility are conducted transparently, equitably, and in compliance with international sustainability and human rights standards — thereby supporting ethical project financing and long-term social sustainability.
client_name: PT Vale New Zealand (supported by International Finance Corporation – IFC)

project_name: ADB TA-9861 INO: Sustainable Infrastructure Assistance Program Phase II - Supporting Sustainable and Universal Electricity Access Phase 2 (Subproject 3)
description:
This technical assistance project under the Asian Development Bank (ADB) TA-9861 INO supports Phase II of the Sustainable Infrastructure Assistance Program (SIAP), focusing on sustainable and universal electricity access across Indonesia. The Environmental and Social Safeguards Firm (JV PT Hatfield Indonesia) is responsible for developing, updating, and harmonizing safeguard instruments across PLN’s national electrification initiatives.

The assignment covers preparation and capacity building on multiple safeguard frameworks, including the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP), Biodiversity Management Plan (BMP), Cultural Heritage Management Plan (CHMP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM). It also involves training PLN staff and regional implementers in the application of ADB’s Safeguard Policy Statement (2009) and national regulations to ensure consistent compliance and accountability.

Through integrated technical support and on-the-ground capacity building, this project strengthens PLN’s institutional readiness to implement energy infrastructure that is environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and aligned with international safeguard standards.
client_name: Asian Development Bank (ADB) and PT PLN (Persero)

project_name: LARAP Preparation and Land Acquisition Implementation for the Development of the Endikat River Hydroelectric Power Plant (HEPP)
description:
This consultancy provides Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) preparation and implementation support for the Endikat River Hydroelectric Power Plant (HEPP) development. The project aims to ensure that land acquisition and resettlement processes are carried out transparently, equitably, and in full compliance with Indonesian regulations and international safeguard standards.

The assignment includes socio-economic and asset surveys, stakeholder consultations, development of compensation frameworks, livelihood restoration programs, and establishment of Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRM) and Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEP). Environmental and social aspects are also assessed through Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Environmental Permit documentation, ensuring that both natural ecosystems and community welfare are protected.

By integrating social safeguard principles into the hydropower development process, this project supports PT Energi Banyu Kencana (EBK) in delivering clean energy infrastructure that is not only technically sound but also socially responsible, environmentally sustainable, and aligned with inclusive development goals across Indonesia’s key island regions.
client_name: PT Energi Banyu Kencana (EBK)

project_name: Construction Management Consultant Services for Bara Lestari Housing Development I – Phase II (SPPH-11925.1)
description:
This project provides construction management consultancy services for the Bara Lestari Housing Development I – Phase II, a residential project initiated by PT Bukit Asam Tbk to support community and employee housing needs near its operational area in South Sumatra.

The consultancy covers supervision and coordination of all construction activities, including scheduling, quality control, safety management, and compliance with technical and environmental standards. The scope also involves monitoring contractor performance, verifying material specifications, and ensuring timely and efficient project delivery in accordance with the approved design and budget.

Through professional management and technical oversight, the project aims to ensure that the Bara Lestari Housing complex is developed to high construction standards, supporting sustainable, safe, and livable housing infrastructure for the local community and company employees.
client_name: PT Bukit Asam Tbk

project_name: Consultation Services on Socialization (Public Consultation) to Fishermen for the Cirata Floating Solar Power Plant Project (2021) – IFC
description:
This consultancy provided public consultation and community engagement services for fishermen affected by the Cirata Floating Solar Power Plant Project, developed under IFC’s environmental and social safeguard framework. The main objective was to facilitate transparent communication, gather feedback, and ensure meaningful participation of local fishing communities around the Cirata Reservoir in West Java.

Activities included stakeholder mapping, preparation of consultation materials, facilitation of public meetings, documentation of community concerns, and development of a summary report with recommendations for integrating fishermen’s input into the project’s Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

Through this engagement, the project strengthened mutual understanding between developers and local stakeholders, promoting inclusive, socially responsible, and sustainable renewable energy development in line with IFC Performance Standards.
client_name: PT Pembangkitan Jawa Bali Masdar Solar Energi

project_name: AA-P167568-ASA-TF0A7983 – Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA): Country Safeguard Framework Assessment (CSFA)
description:
This technical assistance under the World Bank’s Advisory Services and Analytics (ASA) program focuses on conducting a Country Safeguard Framework Assessment (CSFA) to evaluate Indonesia’s existing environmental and social safeguard systems. The objective is to assess their alignment with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and identify key gaps, strengths, and areas for capacity enhancement.

The assessment covers the legal and institutional structures governing land acquisition, resettlement, indigenous peoples, environmental management, and stakeholder engagement. It also provides policy recommendations and an implementation roadmap for harmonizing Indonesia’s safeguard framework with international standards, while strengthening national institutions’ ability to manage environmental and social risks in infrastructure and development projects.

By providing analytical insights and strategic guidance, this project supports Indonesia’s ongoing efforts toward sustainable, inclusive, and safeguard-compliant development governance under the World Bank’s partnership program.
client_name: The World Bank – Jakarta Office

project_name: UKL-UPL Application Document Preparation Services for Forest Area Utilization Permit (PPPKH) – PT DMP Gold Mining Exploration Activities (PT Woyla Aceh Minerals, JV with PT Ayamaru Bakti Pertiwi)
description:
This consultancy provides Environmental Document Preparation Services (UKL-UPL) to support the Forest Area Utilization Permit (PPPKH) application for gold mining exploration activities operated by PT DMP under PT Woyla Aceh Minerals, in joint venture with PT Ayamaru Bakti Pertiwi.

The assignment involves preparing environmental management (UKL) and environmental monitoring (UPL) documents in accordance with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK) and provincial permitting requirements. The study assesses potential environmental impacts of exploration works, including land clearing, access road development, and drilling activities within the designated forest area.

By ensuring compliance with environmental regulations and PPPKH requirements, this project enables the client to obtain the necessary permits for exploration while promoting responsible mineral resource management, environmental protection, and sustainable forestry practices in Aceh Province.
client_name: PT Woyla Aceh Minerals

project_name: TA-8484 INO: Sustainable Infrastructure Assistance Program – Technical Assistance Cluster Management Facility (Subproject 1) – Capacity Development Specialist (46380-003)
description:
This technical assistance project under ADB’s Sustainable Infrastructure Assistance Program (SIAP) focuses on strengthening the institutional capacity of Indonesia’s infrastructure agencies to plan and implement projects in compliance with environmental and social safeguard standards. As the Capacity Development Specialist, the consultancy provides advisory and training support to enhance the understanding and application of safeguard instruments including the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

The assignment involves designing training modules, conducting workshops for central and regional implementing agencies, and developing operational guidelines for safeguard integration into infrastructure project cycles. It also supports knowledge sharing between ADB and national counterparts to align Indonesia’s safeguard practices with international standards.

Through this initiative, ADB’s SIAP program helps advance sustainable, inclusive, and safeguard-compliant infrastructure development, reinforcing good governance and environmental responsibility across Indonesia’s public investment portfolio.
client_name: Asian Development Bank (ADB)

project_name: Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) for Pokko Hydroelectric Power Plant – World Bank
description:
This consultancy focuses on the preparation of a comprehensive Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) for the Pokko Hydroelectric Power Plant (HEPP) in West and South Sulawesi, funded under the World Bank’s safeguard framework. The study ensures that all land acquisition, resettlement, and livelihood restoration processes adhere to World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 5 (ESS5) and are implemented transparently, equitably, and in consultation with affected communities.

The assignment covers socio-economic and asset surveys, stakeholder engagement and consultations, identification of project-affected persons (PAPs), formulation of the Livelihood Restoration Plan (LRP), and the establishment of Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP). Special attention is given to Indigenous Peoples (IP) considerations, ensuring that mitigation measures are culturally appropriate and inclusive.

Through this LARAP, PLN and the World Bank aim to ensure that the Pokko HEPP is developed in a socially responsible and sustainable manner — balancing clean energy generation with fair compensation, community participation, and long-term livelihood security for affected households.

project_name: Pomalaa High Pressure Acid Leach (HPAL) Nickel Project
description:
The Preparation of a Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action Plan (LARAP) for the Pomalaa HPAL Nickel Project was undertaken as a critical component to ensure that land acquisition processes are conducted in a structured, transparent, and socially responsible manner. The LARAP serves as a key instrument to manage potential impacts arising from land acquisition, including displacement, loss of assets, and livelihood disruptions, while ensuring fair and equitable treatment of affected communities.

This LARAP was developed in alignment with applicable Indonesian regulations as well as international standards, particularly the IFC Performance Standard 5 on Land Acquisition and Involuntary Resettlement. By integrating both national and global frameworks, the plan aims to meet compliance requirements while also adopting best practices in safeguarding the rights and well-being of affected persons.

The scope of the LARAP includes a comprehensive set of activities designed to provide an accurate and accountable basis for implementation. These include detailed census surveys to identify affected households and individuals, asset inventory and valuation processes to determine the extent of losses, and structured stakeholder consultations to ensure inclusive participation and transparency. In addition, the plan establishes a clear compensation framework that outlines eligibility criteria, entitlement matrix, and payment mechanisms in a fair and consistent manner.

Beyond compensation, the LARAP emphasizes livelihood restoration measures to support affected communities in re-establishing or improving their socio-economic conditions. This reflects a shift from a purely compensatory approach to a more sustainable development-oriented framework. The plan also incorporates a grievance redress mechanism, enabling affected stakeholders to raise concerns and seek resolution through a structured and accessible process.

Furthermore, the LARAP defines institutional arrangements and implementation strategies, including roles and responsibilities, monitoring and evaluation systems, and reporting mechanisms to ensure accountability throughout the project lifecycle. These elements are essential to ensure that the commitments outlined in the plan are effectively translated into practice.

Overall, the preparation of the LARAP for the Pomalaa HPAL Nickel Project demonstrates a strong commitment to responsible land acquisition and social risk management. It reinforces the importance of balancing project development objectives with the protection of community rights, contributing to more sustainable and socially inclusive project outcomes.

location: Kolaka Regency, Pomalaa District, Southeast Sulawesi Province
